report:
Antecedentes Clínicos:
Obs. Rotura meniscal lateral.
Hallazgos:
Médula ósea de intensidad de señal normal.
Ligamentos cruzados y colaterales sin alteraciones.
Menisco lateral de morfología y señal normal sin criterios categóricos de rotura.
Menisco medial de morfología normal sin criterios de rotura.
Alteración de señal y disminución del espesor del cartílago femorotibial lateral en el tercio medio
de la superficie de carga con defecto de espesor subtotal, mayor a 50% a nivel del platillo tibial
lateral, sin edema óseo. Hallazgos similares con defectos de espesor parcial y subtotal a nivel del
compartimento femorotibial medial.
Cartílago patelofemoral con alteración difusa de señal a nivel de la patela con defectos de espesor
mayor a 50% a nivel de la faceta medial cercano al vértice. Cartílago de la tróclea sin defectos
condrales significativos.
Leves cambios inflamatorios paracondilares externos adyacentes a la banda iliotibial.
Tendón del cuádriceps, rotuliano, de la pata de ganso, bicipital y banda iliotibial de grosor e
intensidad de señal normales.
No se observa derrame articular ni quiste de Baker. Edema del tejido adiposo prefemoral en su
aspecto lateral.
Impresión:
Condropatía femorotibial bicompartimental grado 2-3 con foco de condropatía profunda grado 3 en
el platillo tibial lateral.
Condropatía rotuliana grado 3.
Signos de fricción de la banda iliotibial.
Edema de la grasa pre femoral en su aspecto lateral, puede estar en contexto de un síndrome de
fricción

The study reveals normal knee joint alignment.   No fracture is seen.  
   Mild hyperintense articular cartilaginous at the medial and lateral patellar facet with focal partial thickness cartilage defect, about 14mm., at medial patellar facet with mild suchondral bone edema.   
  Medial and lateral patellar retinacula are preserved.    Minimal PF joint effusion is seen.  
    Quadriceps and patellar tendons are intact.  
 MCL is intact.   Normal shape with preserved signal of medial meniscus is observed. 
 FCL, popliteus and biceps femoris tendons are preserved.  Lateral meniscus is not torn. 
   Normal ACL orientation with intact ligament fiber is observed.  The PCL is intact.  
    Minimal PF joint effusion is seen.  Chondromalacia patella with focal partial thickness cartilage defect, about 14mm., at medial patellar facet,  grade III (modified Outerbridge grading), with mild subchondral bone edema. 
  Mild reactive PF synovitis

In den vorliegenden Sequenzen unauffällige Signalgebung der ossären Strukturen, kein Knochenmarksödem, kein bone bruise. Oberflächliche Chondropathie im medialen sowie lateralen Kompartiment, lateral führend, an der Trochlea (exemplarisch 7/15) und retropatellar. Kein Anhalt für eine Rissbildung des Innen- sowie Außenmeniskus. Mukoide Degeneration der Menisci. VKB und HKB intakt. MCL und LCL intakt. Geringer Gelenkerguss. Quadriceps- sowie Patellarsehne mit intakter Darstellung. Die miterfassten Weichteile in den vorliegenden Sequenzen mit unauffälliger Signalgebung.

MRI LEFT KNEE:

INDICATION:    [Age] female with trauma during ski accident 1.5 weeks ago with persistent pain, swelling and limited range of motion of left knee.

PRIOR IMAGING: None.
.
TECHNICAL INFORMATION AND PROTOCOL:

Proton density and T2 weighted sagittal, coronal and axial imaging was performed through the knee including a 3D Fat suppressed proton density weighted sequence. No contrast was administered.

FINDINGS:

The 3-D proton density sequence was reformatted and manipulated to aid in the interpretation of this examination.

There is a complete tear of the midportion of the anterior cruciate ligament. No normal intact fibers are identified. There is a borderline anterior tibial drawer measured in the lateral joint compartment at about 5 mm. There are bone contusions seen at the lateral femoral sulcus in the posterior aspect of the lateral tibial plateau consistent with kissing contusions related to a pivot shift mechanism of injury. There is a discrete region of linear low T1 signal along the posterior rim of the lateral tibial plateau which may indicate presence of an undisplaced lateral tibial plateau rim fracture.

The posterior cruciate ligament is intact.

There is abnormal signal surrounding the medial collateral ligament at its origin along its course proximal to the medial joint line consistent with grade 2 sprain. There is significant disruption of the deep fibers with intact superficial fibers extending distally. The posterior oblique ligament appears intact. There is an associated partial thickness sprain of the femoral insertion of the medial patellofemoral ligament.

The lateral collateral ligament complex is intact. There is some subtle increased signal seen in the proximal fibers of the fibular collateral ligament which could indicate presence of a low-grade sprain. The fibular collateral ligament, IT band, biceps femoris tendon and popliteus tendon appear intact.

There is abnormal increased T2 signal seen in the periphery of the medial meniscus involving posterior horn and body consistent with a meniscocapsular avulsion injury. No discrete surfacing meniscal tear is identified to the medial meniscus. The articular cartilage of the medial joint compartment is well-maintained.

The lateral meniscus is intact. The articular cartilage of the lateral joint compartment is well-maintained.

The extensor mechanism is intact. The lateral patellofemoral ligament is unremarkable. As noted the medial patellofemoral ligament at its femoral insertion demonstrates a partial thickness sprain. The articular cartilage of the patellofemoral joint is reasonably well-maintained apart from some mild fissuring seen to the trochlear articular cartilage at the apex and involving the medial facet. Findings are consistent with moderate chondrosis.

No significant Baker's cyst is demonstrated.

There is a moderate to large knee effusion.

INTERPRETATION:
 
Complete anterior cruciate ligament tear with bone contusions corresponding to a pivot shift mechanism of injury and with possible undisplaced posterior tibial plateau fracturing. Plain film correlation is recommended.

Grade 2 medial collateral ligament sprain associated with partial-thickness sprain of the insertional fibers of the medial patellofemoral ligament.

Evidence of meniscocapsular injury to the medial meniscus involving posterior horn and body with no discrete surfacing tear identified.

Moderate chondromalacia patella.

Moderate knee effusion.

MRI LEFT KNEE  (plain)

Clinical information:
Rule out loose body or bucket handle meniscal tear. Recurrent locking and instability. 

Technique: 
Multiplanar MR of the knee according to protocol.

Comparison: 
None

Findings: 

Menisci

Lateral meniscus: No meniscal tear. No para meniscal cyst.

Medial meniscus: Horizontal tear of the posterior horn and body with extension to the inferior articular surface. Meniscal extrusion of approximately 0.3 cm.

Ligaments

Anterior cruciate ligament: intact

Posterior cruciate ligament: intact 

Medial collateral ligament: Superficial and deep components intact. No periligamentous edema.

Lateral collateral ligament: The iliotibial band, biceps femoris tendon, fibular collateral ligament and popliteus muscle and tendon intact. 

Posterolateral corner structures: Intact

Extensor Mechanism

The distal quadriceps and patellar tendons are intact. The patella is normally positioned within the femoral groove. There is no retinacular disruption.

Fluid

Small joint effusion. No loose body. No Baker's cyst.

Osseous and Articular Structures

Bones: A 0.8cm x 0.9cm x 0.8cm intraosseous ganglion is seen at the medial femur. No fracture, stress reaction, or osseous lesion is seen.

Patellofemoral compartment: Minimal chondrosis.

Medial compartment: Minimal chondrosis.

Lateral compartment: Minimal chondrosis. 

Others:

Hoffa's fat pad: clear

Muscles: No abnormal oedema. 

Neurovascular bundle: Normal 


COMMENT
Horizontal tear of the posterior horn and body of the medial meniscus with extension to the inferior articular surface, resulting in meniscal extrusion of approximately 0.3 cm.

No evidence of loose body or bucket-handle meniscal tear. Cruciate ligaments appear intact.

Interprétation :

Minime liséré de liquide au sein du récessus supra-patellaire sans épanchement intra-articulaire significatif. Kyste de Baker multi-lobulé et allongé s’étendant jusqu’à 8cm de diamètre CC. Pas d’évidence de complication ou signe de rupture.

Légère anomalie de signal linéaire iso-intense d’allure horizontale longitudinale s’étendant de la corne postérieure au corps méniscal et impliquant la surface articulaire supérieure, suggérant une déchirure d’allure chronique. Minimes changements dégénératifs mucoïdes par ailleurs.

Le ligament collatéral interne est intact sans déchirure. 

Légère atténuation des surfaces chondrales au compartiment fémoro-tibial interne sans atteinte transfixiante.

Petite déchirure radiaire partielle focale au rebord libre à la jonction de la corne antérieure et du corps du ménisque externe. Le complexe ligamentaire collatéral externe est intact sans déchirure.

Légère atténuation des surfaces chondrales, en particulier la surface portante du compartiment fémoro-tibial externe sans atteinte transfixiante.

Les ligaments croisés antérieur et postérieur sont intacts sans déchirure. Petit kyste ganglionnaire intra-osseux sous l’insertion distale du ligament croisé antérieur.

Artéfacts de susceptibilité magnétique en projection du rétinaculum interne et des tissus sous-cutanés. À corréler cliniquement. Est-ce qu’il y a déjà eu une intervention chirurgicale locale à ce niveau ?

La rotule est hautement située avec une légère patella alta suspectée. Il y a un petit foyer d’œdème au versant supéro-externe de la graisse de Hoffa suggérant un syndrome de friction du tendon patellaire et du condyle fémoral externe.

Il y a une atténuation diffuse modérée des surfaces cartilagineuses au compartiment patellofémoral avec une atteinte transfixiante le long de l’apex patellaire et de la facette patellaire externe, avec changements réactionnels sous-chondraux associés, en lien avec une chondropathie sévère. Petits ostéophytes marginaux au compartiment patellofémoral avec petit kyste adjacent à l’extrémité externe de la facette trochléaire externe.

Légère tendinose du quadriceps distal sans déchirure. Le tendon patellaire est intact sans déchirure.

Conclusion :

Déchirure longitudinale horizontale d’allure chronique à la corne postérieure et au corps du ménisque interne.

Petite déchirure focale radiaire au rebord libre à la jonction de la corne antérieure et du corps du ménisque externe.

Légère chondropathie au compartiment fémoro-tibial interne et externe.

Chondropathie modérée à sévère au compartiment patellofémoral avec atteinte sévère, transfixiante à l’apex patellaire et le long de la facette patellaire externe tel que détaillé ci-haut.

Légère patella alta suspectée avec petit foyer d’œdème au versant supéro-externe de la graisse de Hoffa suggérant un syndrome d’accrochage de la graisse de Hoffa/syndrome de friction du tendon patellaire et du condyle fémoral externe.

Pas d’épanchement intra-articulaire significatif. Kyste de Baker allongé non-compliqué tel que décrit ci-haut.

FINDINGS:

Fluid:
Mild interval reduction in moderate joint effusion. No popliteal cyst.

Medial compartment (meniscus, collateral ligament, cartilage):
Unchanged multidirectional tear of the posterior horn of the medial meniscus, with longitudinal horizontal and complete radial components. Unchanged mild meniscal extrusion. Unchanged displacement of the posterior medial meniscal root into the medial aspect of the intercondylar notch. This represents an unstable meniscal tear.
Normal medial collateral ligament. Partial-thickness fissuring of medial compartment articular cartilage.

Lateral compartment (meniscus, collateral ligament complex, cartilage):
Normal meniscus. Normal lateral collateral ligament complex. Unchanged partial-thickness chondral fissuring within the lateral compartment.

Intercondylar compartment (anterior and posterior cruciate ligaments):
Unchanged complete tear of the anterior cruciate ligament. There is approximately 9 mm of anterior tibial translation. Normal posterior cruciate ligament.

Anterior compartment (extensor mechanism, cartilage, Hoffa's fat pad):
Partial-thickness chondral fissuring within the medial and lateral patellar facet articular cartilage.
Normal extensor mechanism. Normal fat pads.

Bones:
Interval resolution of bone marrow edema previously seen within the posterolateral tibial plateau

Muscles and neurovascular structures:
Small T1 hyperintense fluid collection within the muscle belly of the medial head of gastrocnemius measuring maximally up to 1 cm in craniocaudal dimension, is likely a small intramuscular hematoma.

Other findings:
None

CONCLUSION:
1.No significant interval change other than for resolution of posterolateral tibial plateau bone marrow edema compared to the previous MRI.
2.Complete tear of the anterior cruciate ligament.
3.Unchanged unstable tear of the posterior horn of the medial meniscus, with displacement of the posterior medial meniscal root into the medial intercondylar notch.
